## Natural history notes

A small lady beetle characterized by a rounded, glossy body, dark coloration, and reddish to orange markings, sometimes giving it a “little red lady beetle” appearance. In Florida, Exochomus childreni is one of the state’s native lady beetles, recorded especially from central and northern Florida and also included in Florida’s listed Exochomus fauna. Adults and larvae are predatory, feeding on small soft-bodied insects such as aphids, scales, and psyllid nymphs, making them beneficial insects in gardens, citrus, forest edges, and other plant-rich habitats.
